The proposition

A measurable London service—without rebuilding the itinerary or your app.

  • Starts from the actual hotel and free-time window
  • Delivered through email, WhatsApp, vouchers or the tour leader
  • Attributed by product, departure, property and channel
One guest link · one attributable journey
One use case

Turn two free hours before dinner into a confident choice.

01

Distribute in context

The customer opens a departure-specific link from the itinerary, pre-departure message or tour leader. The product, hotel and channel are already known.

02

Add their intent

They choose the time available and how they want London to feel. The result is in Italian and starts from the programme hotel.

03

Act—and attribute it

Directions, route building and feedback become measurable events attached to that product and departure, without using a passenger name.

For the traveller: a useful answer for the part of the trip the fixed itinerary cannot cover.

For the operator: a differentiated service layer that can be tested on one product and repeated across departures.

Technical attribution

Every signal retains its commercial context.

Each QR code or short link resolves to a controlled combination of identifiers. Every subsequent event inherits the same attribution envelope.

POCOP-DEMO
→
ProductLON-CITY-4D
→
DepartureDEP-03NOV
→
PropertyBLOOM-01
→
ChannelLEADER-WA
What is recorded

Anonymous session ID, event, timestamp, selected time and mood, content variant and the five attribution identifiers above.

What is not required

No passenger name, email, booking reference, passport information, CRM access or passenger manifest is needed for the base pilot.

What the operator supplies

Eligible passenger counts, confirmed departures and whether each agreed channel was actually used. These provide the denominators digital analytics cannot invent.

The 90-day pilot

One product. Up to five departures. A commercial decision.

The pilot tests whether customers use the companion, act on its recommendations and recognise it as part of the operator’s service—not whether a demo page can attract clicks.

Controlled scope 1 London product 3–5 departures Up to 300 passengers Up to 3 London hotels
Days 1–14Map and instrument

Choose the product, departures and channels. Map hotels and genuine free-time windows; configure Italian content, co-branding, identifiers, events and the frozen measurement plan.

Days 15–30Launch

Prepare links and QR assets for the itinerary, email, WhatsApp and tour leader. Brief the operating team, launch the first departure and verify the attribution chain.

Days 31–75Compare and improve

Review results by departure and channel every two weeks. Test one distribution or message variable at a time while leaving the success definition unchanged.

Days 76–90Decide

Deliver event data, customer and team feedback, operating lessons, production economics and a clear recommendation: stop, iterate or scale.

Included
  • Co-branded Italian traveller experience

The base pilot does not require an app, login, booking-engine integration or personally identifiable passenger data.

Five decision signals

A result tied to departures—not aggregate page traffic.

SignalDefinitionRead byProposed gate
ReachUnique anonymous opens ÷ passengers sent the linkDeparture + channel≥30%
CompletionRecommendations received ÷ experience startsProduct + hotel≥50%
ActionDirection, route or save taps ÷ completed flowsDeparture + property≥30%
UsefulnessPositive responses ÷ all feedback responsesContent variant≥70%
Distribution adoptionEligible departures where the agreed link was distributedTeam + channel≥80%

Denominator rule: reach is calculated only where the operator confirms how many passengers actually received the link. A passenger manifest is neither requested nor uploaded.

Honest constraint: a directions tap shows intent, not a completed visit. These thresholds are proposed decision gates, not claimed travel-industry benchmarks.
